findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of shell interpolation
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `HEAD; malicious-command`, `exec` runs the additional command with the application's privileges. Metacharacters in legitimate ref names can also alter process behavior. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` invocation passed the value literally and avoided shell interpretation.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the Git process lifecycle for branch names containing `&`
findings.body:
`&` is valid in Git branch names but is interpreted by POSIX shells as the background operator. `showBranch("topic&")` therefore backgrounds `git show topic`; the returned shell process can exit successfully before Git finishes, causing premature completion signals and preventing cancellation of the actual Git process.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` evaluates `branch` as shell syntax. Any caller-provided value such as `HEAD; malicious-command` executes an additional command with the application's privileges; valid Git refs containing shell metacharacters are also misinterpreted. The previous `execFile` call passed the value literally.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an `execFile` argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so attacker-controlled branch input such as `HEAD; touch /tmp/pwn` executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of executing it through a shell
findings.body:
A caller-controlled branch such as `HEAD >/dev/null; while :; do :; done` is interpreted by the shell, consuming a CPU core indefinitely; repeated calls can exhaust CPU and process capacity. `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` treated the value only as a Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
